comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 Compas curriculum; Fall 2026 entrant pathway, checked 2026-10-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The 180 EC Compas pathway comprises 156 EC of compulsory major study, including the 6 EC thesis, and a 24 EC minor. The existing 27 components retain 60 EC in each year. Amsterdam Global Health is the first-listed faculty minor, selected neutrally; it studies local primary/community care, social determinants, diversity and participatory projects. It is a minor choice, not a graduation specialization, and selection, capacity and annual availability apply. External minors require approval, a coherent nonoverlapping university programme of at least 24 EC, at most 6 EC at level 100 and at least 12 EC at level 300; placements cannot fill this minor. The additional 6 EC minor thesis applies only to visiting non-Medicine students and is not added here. Year-2 entry requires the first-year study-advice threshold of 42 EC. Year-3 entry requires all Year 1 and 30 EC from Year 2; minor entry additionally requires at least 18 EC from semester 2.1. Care-placement preparation must be passed or equivalent knowledge accepted by the examiner. General-practice placement requires sufficient professional behavior in the care placement and approval by the Medical Expert examiner. Confidentiality must be signed before patient-related teaching. Practical work, study groups and placements require attendance and participation. The Dutch diagnostic/remedial language pass gates Doctor and Patient 1; professional behavior, portfolios, immediate knowledge, skills/first-aid and final progress assessments are embedded pass conditions, not extra credit units. Embedded research introductions belong to Doctor and Patient 2/4; general-practice work belongs to Medical Expert 4 within Doctor and Patient 4. The care placement carries 6 EC once. The compulsory thesis is the nonexempt final work of the major, after the minor in semester 3.1. Current course guidance specifies a short systematic review or, for research-minor students, a report of their own study: about 3000–5000 words in scientific English, an initial proposal, individual supervision and weekly meetings/writing sessions. Students arrange and register a suitable supervisor and tentative subject before their course starts, using Canvas instructions. The current January 2027 registration date concerns current Year-3 students; it is not imposed on the Fall 2026 entrant’s future Year 3. The thesis is graded at least 6.0 after all obligations are met. This comparison uses the 2026–2027 Compas rules for Fall 2026 entrants. VUMED360 starts in September 2027 and cannot absorb Compas credits. The last full teaching years are 2026–2027 for Year 1, 2027–2028 for Year 2 and 2028–2029 for Year 3; no regular Compas teaching follows August 2029. The final graduation deadline is 31 August 2030. The transition appendix governs remaining assessments and exceptional opportunities; it also provides an individual delayed-study-advice decision for affected entrants. Later annual offerings and minor placement must be checked.
components: First-listed 24 EC faculty minor; local primary/community health, diversity, social determinants and participatory community projects. Admission/selection/capacity and annual availability apply; not a formal degree route.

Compulsory 6 EC final major thesis after the minor; systematic review or eligible research-minor report in scientific English, individually supervised. It is not an additional visiting-student minor thesis.

alternatives.label: Biomedicine, neuroscience & health psychology
alternatives.concept: Investigate human function, molecular and organ-system disease, pharmacology, brain function and the psychological experience of illness, using laboratory, statistical and research-synthesis methods. This offers substantial biomedical and psychological study related to Medicine, while patient examination, clinical reasoning in practice and medical professional formation remain outside the programme.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has substantial biomedical, cognitive and clinical-psychology sequences; the label avoids suggesting a full Medicine curriculum.
progression: All actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings pass for 24 unique courses, 180 EC, four each semester, at least six advanced courses and Year-1 PPD. Gateways precede dependent courses; methods precede advanced statistics and synthesis, cell biology/biochemistry precede laboratory/disease study, and abnormal psychology precedes psychodiagnostics in the primary programme. The secondary contemporary social-theory course has no formal prerequisite; its advisory modern-sociology reference was considered, with introductory sociology and qualitative inquiry before it. No extra hard constraint is invented.

alternatives.label: Biomedicine, population health & social inclusion
alternatives.concept: Retain substantial biomedical study while investigating health risks, social influences on illness, diversity, rights and community participation. Population-health evidence, qualitative inquiry and a civil-society project support this direction; rights and sociology are specific social complements, not clinical care or specialist health-law training.
alternatives.labelReason: Biomedicine remains the foundation, while social psychology, qualitative research, civil-society inquiry and rights replace four neurocognitive/therapeutic courses. The social-inclusion emphasis is bounded by actual general social-course content, not a claim to public-health professional preparation.
progression: All actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings pass for 24 unique courses, 180 EC, four each semester, at least six advanced courses and Year-1 PPD. Gateways precede dependent courses; methods precede advanced statistics and synthesis, cell biology/biochemistry precede laboratory/disease study, and abnormal psychology precedes psychodiagnostics in the primary programme. The secondary contemporary social-theory course has no formal prerequisite; its advisory modern-sociology reference was considered, with introductory sociology and qualitative inquiry before it. No extra hard constraint is invented.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each programme: neurobiology, higher cognitive functions, psychodiagnostics/psychotherapies and lifespan psychology are replaced by social psychology, qualitative research, contemporary social theory and human rights. These changes implement the social-inclusion concept rather than arbitrary breadth.

candidates.label: Learning medicine through supervised patient contact

selection.assessment: Two distinct qualified responses are supported by the verified biomedical/psychological core and the exact-target diversity/population-health direction, including the selected minor’s social determinants and community-research content. The second changes four courses/30 EC toward social psychology, qualitative methods, civil society and rights. Supervised patient-contact learning cannot be supplied by academic anatomy, laboratory cases or psychodiagnostics; that candidate remains not feasible. No third programme is manufactured from postgraduate careers or illustrative activities.

blocks: Both examine skeletal/body structure and function. UCR uses surface anatomy, imaging and anatomical materials as academic learning; VU additionally teaches musculoskeletal clinical reasoning, history-taking and physical examination.

Both study host-pathogen interactions, immune and inflammatory mechanisms. VU additionally develops clinical presentations, antimicrobial treatment, dermatology and rheumatology; the courses differ in scope and credits.

Both examine cardiovascular pathophysiology as a central organ-system subject. UCR surveys six systems; VU additionally develops cardiovascular diagnosis, treatment, vascular procedures and clinical communication.

Both study homeostasis, control and integrated human function. VU specifically develops autonomic/endocrine systems, pharmacological applications and clinical examples; UCR explicitly remains general human physiology.

Nutrient metabolism and the biochemical regulation of carbohydrates, fats and proteins form an important shared subject. VU additionally integrates respiratory/digestive anatomy, physiology, disease and clinical examination.
Both directly study cell/tissue injury, inflammation, immune processes and repair. UCR adds molecular genetics; VU integrates clinical disease and immunological dysfunction.

notes.text: VU Medicine integrates human biology and disease mechanisms with clinical reasoning, patient encounters, communication, practical care, medical skills and professional formation. UCR provides substantial related biomedical and psychological study, with a second emphasis on population health and society, but neither programme reproduces those clinical and professional sequences. Anatomy demonstrations, laboratory cases and academic psychodiagnostics are not supervised medical placements or physician training.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Medicine combines human biology and disease mechanisms with clinical reasoning, patient communication, care placements and professional medical formation. This comparison uses the Compas curriculum for Fall 2026 entrants, including a minor and an individual bachelor thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers two qualified related approaches. The first combines biomedicine, neuroscience and health psychology; the second retains biomedical study while adding population health, qualitative inquiry and social inclusion. Both provide substantial study of normal function, disease and research. They do not reproduce the structured medical skills, supervised patient contact, clinical reasoning, care placements or professional assessments in VU Medicine. Comparative animal neurobiology, general ethics, rights and social theory have specific supporting roles. Neither composition is a medical degree, physician qualification or guarantee of admission to a medical master’s programme.

curriculum.limitation: This is the 180 EC Compas pathway for Fall 2026 entrants: 156 EC of compulsory major study, including a 6 EC thesis, plus a 24 EC minor. Amsterdam Global Health illustrates the first-listed faculty minor, subject to admission, selection, capacity and annual availability. It is not a separate degree route. External minor choices require approval and a coherent nonoverlapping university programme; placements cannot fill that space. Year-2 entry requires 42 first-year EC. Year 3 requires all Year 1 and 30 EC from Year 2, with at least 18 EC from semester 2.1 for the minor. Placement preparation, sufficient professional behavior, confidentiality, active attendance and embedded clinical/portfolio/language assessments also apply. The thesis follows the minor and requires individually supervised scientific writing in English; students arrange and register their supervisor and topic before the applicable course starts. The extra visiting-student minor thesis is not counted. Compas is being phased out: regular teaching ends after 2028–2029 and graduation must be completed by 31 August 2030. Compas credits do not transfer into VUMED360, which starts in September 2027.
